findings.claim: Water-carriage opens a more extensive market than land-carriage alone. Smith's comparison: six or eight men in a ship can move two hundred tons London–Leith in the same six weeks it takes fifty broad-wheeled waggons, a hundred men, and four hundred horses to move four tons London–Edinburgh; land transport is only viable for goods whose value is great relative to their weight.

claim.name: Three causes of the productivity gain: dexterity, time-saving, machinery
steps: Check dexterity: will the role involve one simple operation performed repeatedly as a sole employment?
Check switch-time: how much time is currently lost moving between different places, tools, and kinds of work, including slow mental re-engagement?
Check invention potential: will concentrating attention on one simple object make easier methods likely to be found?

findings.claim: Smith holds that the greatest improvements in productive power come from dividing work into distinct trades and simple operations. The pin manufactory example shows an untrained workman might barely make one pin a day alone, while ten specialized workers making ~4,800 pins each per day achieve roughly a 240-fold (or up to 4,800-fold) multiplication of output. Division of labour is carried furthest in the most improved societies, and trades separate from one another because of this advantage.

findings.finding: The source qualifies the reported production capacity with exertion. The saved summary and explanation omit that condition while describing daily output. This is a targeted fidelity concern, not a new measurement of the workshop.

No full-book Flash run, no cross-book generalization measurement, and no end-user skill usefulness evaluation.
